en.heroIntro: Compare Pika 2.2 Text & Image to Video with Wan 2.6 Text & Image to Video when the real choice is a lower-cost short loop or a longer, audio-ready production workflow. Pika keeps simple prompt and image animation economical, while Wan adds 15-second output and reference-video control.

quickVerdict.title: Quick verdict
quickVerdict.body: Choose Pika 2.2 for inexpensive 5- or 10-second silent loops, stylized tests, and straightforward image animation. Choose Wan 2.6 when the shot needs up to 15 seconds, native audio, or one to three reference videos, accepting the higher 720p and 1080p generation price.

topCards.title: Choose Pika 2.2
topCards.body: Use Pika for lower-cost 720p tests, short silent loops, and simple text-to-video or image-to-video work.

topCards.title: Choose Wan 2.6
topCards.body: Use Wan for clips up to 15 seconds, optional audio, 1080p delivery, or a workflow guided by reference videos.

topCards.title: Key trade-off
topCards.body: Pika starts at $0.04 per second at 720p; Wan starts at $0.10 per second but adds duration, audio, and reference-video control.

topCards.title: Best workflows
topCards.body: Pika fits stylized social loops and concept tests. Wan fits longer general-purpose shots, narrated clips, and reference-led sequences.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Short answers for choosing between Pika 2.2 and Wan 2.6.

items.question: Is Pika 2.2 or Wan 2.6 better for low-cost video tests?
items.answer: Pika 2.2 is the lower-cost choice at 720p and works well for short silent loops. Wan 2.6 costs more but is justified when a test needs audio, longer duration, or reference videos.

items.question: What can Wan 2.6 do that Pika 2.2 cannot?
items.answer: Wan 2.6 supports clips up to 15 seconds, optional audio, and a reference-to-video workflow with one to three video references. Pika 2.2 is limited to text-to-video and image-to-video without audio.

items.question: Which model should I use for a polished 1080p clip?
items.answer: Both offer 1080p. Choose Pika for a straightforward silent shot at a lower price, or Wan when the final clip benefits from native audio, extra duration, or reference-video guidance.
